title_en: The four-day week: progress or pressure?
title_he: שבוע עבודה של ארבעה ימים: התקדמות או לחץ?
prompt: Argue whether employers should move to a four-day working week with no reduction in pay, and respond to opposing views.

instructions.en: Write an argumentative essay of 450-550 words for a general reader. This time the support is lighter: plan the essay on your own. State a clear thesis; you may limit it to certain kinds of work (for example, office jobs) if your reasoning leads you there, because a qualified thesis is often stronger than a sweeping one. Develop at least three supporting arguments with evidence, and consider the question from the point of view of at least two groups affected, such as employees, employers and customers. Present the strongest opposing view fairly, rebut it with reasons, and finish with a conclusion that adds no new arguments. Use examples, reasoning and clearly described experience (your own or that of people you know); do not invent statistics.
instructions.he: כתבו חיבור טיעוני באורך 450–550 מילים. הפעם התמיכה מצומצמת יותר: תכננו את החיבור בעצמכם. אפשר לסייג את התזה (למשל, לעבודה משרדית בלבד) אם הנימוקים שלכם מובילים לשם, כי תזה מסויגת היא לעתים קרובות חזקה יותר מתזה גורפת. פתחו לפחות שלושה טיעונים עם ראיות, והתייחסו לפחות לשתי קבוצות שמושפעות מהשינוי (למשל עובדים, מעסיקים, לקוחות). הציגו בהגינות את הטיעון הנגדי החזק ביותר, ענו עליו בנימוקים, וסיימו בסיכום שאינו מוסיף טיעונים חדשים. אל תמציאו נתונים.

required_elements: a clear thesis, qualified if your reasoning requires it
at least three supporting arguments, each with evidence or a specific example
consideration of at least two affected groups (e.g. employees, employers, customers)
the strongest opposing view, stated fairly and attributed
a reasoned rebuttal (refute, concede and outweigh, or qualify)
a conclusion that adds no new arguments

checklist.en: Claim: my thesis is clear and, where my reasoning requires it, limited to the kinds of work or conditions I can defend.
checklist.he: טענה: התזה שלי ברורה, ובמקרה הצורך מוגבלת לסוגי עבודה או לתנאים שאפשר להגן עליהם בנימוקים.

checklist.en: Reasons: I develop at least three reasons and consider at least two groups affected (employees, employers, customers).
checklist.he: נימוקים: פיתחתי לפחות שלושה נימוקים והתייחסתי לפחות לשתי קבוצות שמושפעות מהשינוי (עובדים, מעסיקים, לקוחות).

checklist.en: Evidence: each reason has a specific example or clearly described experience, and I explain the link. No invented numbers.
checklist.he: ראיות: לכל נימוק יש דוגמה ספציפית או ניסיון שמתואר בבירור, והסברתי את הקשר. אין מספרים מומצאים.

checklist.en: Counterargument: I state the strongest opposing view fairly and attribute it.
checklist.he: טיעון נגדי: הצגתי את העמדה הנגדית החזקה ביותר בהגינות וציינתי מי מחזיק בה.

checklist.en: Rebuttal: my rebuttal uses reasons or evidence, not dismissal, and it fits my thesis.
checklist.he: הפרכה: ההפרכה שלי מבוססת על נימוקים או ראיות ולא על דחייה בלי הסבר, והיא מתיישבת עם התזה.

checklist.en: Conclusion: my conclusion restates the thesis in new words and adds no new arguments.
checklist.he: סיכום: הסיכום מנסח את התזה במילים חדשות ואינו מוסיף טיעונים חדשים.

scaffold.en: Before you write, test your thesis: who exactly does it apply to, and what would make it false?
scaffold.he: לפני הכתיבה, בדקו את התזה: על מי בדיוק היא חלה, ומה היה מוכיח שהיא שגויה?

scaffold.en: Plan one line per paragraph, then check that every body paragraph supports the thesis.
scaffold.he: תכננו שורה אחת לכל פסקה, ובדקו שכל פסקת גוף תומכת בתזה.

scaffold.en: After drafting, reread your objection paragraph as someone who disagrees: is it fair, and is your answer a reason rather than a dismissal?
scaffold.he: אחרי הטיוטה, קראו שוב את פסקת הטיעון הנגדי מנקודת המבט של מי שחולק עליכם: האם הצגתם את עמדתו בהגינות, והאם התשובה שלכם היא נימוק ולא דחייה בלי הסבר?

exemplar.outline:
Parallel prompt (not your question; read this only after you have written your own essay): Argue whether secondary schools should give students one afternoon a week for independent projects of their own choice, and respond to opposing views.

Thesis (qualified): Secondary schools should give older students one afternoon a week for independent projects, provided that each student agrees a plan with a mentor and presents the result at the end of term.

1. Introduction (annotated below): context, the proposal, an early mention of the objection, qualified thesis.
2. Argument 1, self-direction: planning a project, setting deadlines and solving problems without step-by-step instructions. Example: a student who builds a simple app for a local club.
3. Argument 2, motivation: choice increases effort; this affects students, and also teachers, who learn what their students care about.
4. Argument 3, discovering interests: subjects the timetable has no room for. Example: recording interviews with grandparents for a local history project.
5. Opposing view and rebuttal: many students would waste the time. Concede that unstructured time can be wasted; answer with the mentor plan and the end-of-term presentation; point out that the qualification in the thesis exists because of this objection.
6. Conclusion: restate the thesis; suggest starting with one year group.
exemplar.annotated_paragraph:
From the exemplar essay on the parallel prompt above (paragraph 1: introduction)

[1] In most secondary schools, almost every hour of the week is planned by someone other than the student. [2] Some educators now propose giving students one afternoon a week to work on an independent project of their own choice, such as building an app, researching local history or learning an instrument. [3] Critics worry that, without a teacher's structure, many students would simply waste the time. [4] This risk is real, but it is an argument for supervising the afternoon well, not for abandoning the idea. [5] Secondary schools should give older students one afternoon a week for independent projects, provided that each student agrees a plan with a mentor and presents the result at the end of term, because this would build self-direction, increase motivation and let students discover interests that the timetable leaves no room for.

Notes
[1] Sets the context with a specific observation instead of a cliché such as "Nowadays...".
[2] Explains the proposal precisely, with examples, so the reader knows exactly what is being argued about.
[3] Mentions the main objection early, which tells the reader the essay will be balanced.
[4] Previews the rebuttal in one sentence; the full answer comes later in the essay.
[5] Qualified thesis: "older students" and "provided that..." limit the claim to what the essay can defend. The three reasons preview the body paragraphs in order.
